findings.title: Revoke existing local recovery codes when saving a new set externally
findings.body: When a federated user already has recovery codes in Keycloak storage—for example, codes enrolled before this change—a successful external update skips credential creation without removing the existing local credential. Credential validation can still fall back to the local provider when external validation rejects an input, so codes from the replaced set remain usable after regeneration. Remove the previous local recovery credential after successfully saving the replacement externally, and cover this migration case with a regression test.

findings.title: Remove exhausted recovery credentials from the correct storage
findings.body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by a user-storage provider, but this cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which removes credentials from Keycloak's local/federated database rather than disabling the external provider's credential. An exhausted external credential therefore remains present. If the user abandons the required re-enrollment, a provider that reports configuration based on credential existence will still select recovery authentication on the next login, where getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() fails because every code is used. Route exhausted external credentials through the user-storage disabling mechanism instead.

findings.title: Make the recovery-code fixture consume successful inputs
findings.body: The new validator accepts any code in the original list but never consumes it, and getCredentials reconstructs an entirely unused recovery credential from that list on every call. Consequently, the added login test passes while the fixture keeps requesting code zero, permits replay indefinitely, and can never exercise exhaustion or forced re-enrollment. Persist consumption in the fixture and test used-code rejection, advancement to the next code, and exhaustion so the external-storage recovery lifecycle is actually covered.
